discussions.title: What are you guarding?
discussions.body:
nominee is useful when an agent can change real data — refunds, merges, forwards, deletes — and you want a rule to fire **before** the tool function runs.

If you are evaluating the library, this thread is the place to say what tool you need to gate.

Useful shape:

- Framework (AI SDK, Eve, OpenAI Agents, Mastra, MCP, something else)
- One tool name you would deny or `ask` on
- Whether a human has to approve, or a static deny is enough

If your agent is read-only, you probably do not need nominee — say so; that is a valid outcome.

Runnable proof with no signup: `npx nominee-cli`
Docs: https://nominee.dev/docs/

discussions.title: Which framework should we adapt next?
discussions.body:
Official adapters today: `nominee-ai`, `nominee-eve`, `nominee-openai`, `nominee-mastra`, `nominee-mcp`. Each routes through `nominee.run()` so authorization is bound to the exact arguments.

This thread is for **the next adapter**, not a rewrite of the core.

Please include:

- Framework name and the tool primitive it already has (`tool()`, `createTool`, …)
- Whether it has a native approval/resume API we should record as `frameworkApproval` instead of asking twice
- A link to a minimal official example

LangChain JS is a frequent request; there is no official adapter yet. If that is what you need, say so here rather than opening an issue until we have a concrete `run()` mapping.

Core stays dependency-free — adapters live in their own packages.

discussions.title: How do I bind an approval to the exact tool arguments?
discussions.body:
If you `authorize()` in one place and execute later with a mutated `amount` or `to`, you have an unbound decision.

**Answer:** use `nominee.run()` (or `prepareAction` → `executeCapability`). The capability is bound to a canonical hash of the input. Changing arguments after approval throws `AuthorizationInputChangedError` instead of executing.

```ts
await nominee.run(
  { tool: 'refund.issue', input: { orderId, amount }, user },
  async ({ input, token }) => issueRefund(input, token),
)
```

`production: true` disables unbound `authorize()` / `token()` on purpose.

Deeper: https://nominee.dev/docs/ and `packages/core/src/action.ts`.

If that still does not match your runtime, reply with the adapter and where the tool `execute` lives.

discussions.title: Share a policy that surprised you
discussions.body:
First matching rule wins; unmatched calls fall back to `ask` unless you set `fallback: 'deny'`. Sub-agent policies can only narrow.

Paste a redacted policy that did something you did not expect — a `when` predicate that never fired, a `max` budget that escalated, a deny that was shadowed by an earlier `allow('*')`.

`npx nominee-cli check policy.mjs` only checks tool-name reachability against a built-in sample list; it does not execute `when`. That is a known limitation (and a good first issue).

Keep customer data and tokens out of the paste.

issues.title: Add and/or/not helpers for policy `when` predicates
issues.body:
## Why

`when` is a raw function. Combining two input checks means nested `&&` / `||` at every call site. Small, composable helpers would make policies readable without changing evaluation order.

## Pointer

- Implement in [`packages/core/src/policy.ts`](packages/core/src/policy.ts)
- Export from [`packages/core/src/index.ts`](packages/core/src/index.ts)
- Tests in [`packages/core/test/policy.test.ts`](packages/core/test/policy.test.ts)

Core must stay dependency-free.

## Acceptance criterion

```ts
allow('email.forward', {
  when: and(
    ({ input }) => String(input?.to ?? '').endsWith('@acme.com'),
    not(({ input }) => Boolean(input?.bcc)),
  ),
})
```

- `and` / `or` / `not` accept the same `when` signature (sync or async) and return a `when` function.
- Tests cover: all true, one false, async predicates, and that a non-matching `when` still falls through to the next rule.
- `pnpm --filter nominee test` passes.

Do not change first-match-wins semantics.

issues.title: Add input-amount / allowlist predicate helpers + tests
issues.body:
## Why

The refund proof repeats `({ input }) => (input?.amount ?? 0) <= 50`. A tiny helper for numeric ceilings and string allowlists would make first policies copy-pasteable without teaching the whole `ToolCall` type.

## Pointer

- [`packages/core/src/policy.ts`](packages/core/src/policy.ts)
- Tests: [`packages/core/test/policy.test.ts`](packages/core/test/policy.test.ts)
- Keep examples in comments aligned with [`packages/cli/src/proof.ts`](packages/cli/src/proof.ts)

## Acceptance criterion

Helpers along the lines of:

- `lte('amount', 50)` — reads a numeric field off `input`, missing/NaN is false
- `inList('to', ['finance@acme.com'])` — string field must be in the list

Each helper is a `when` predicate. Tests include missing field, wrong type, and a full `PolicyEngine.evaluate` that allows then denies. No new runtime dependencies.

issues.title: `nominee check`: report rules shadowed by an earlier matching pattern
issues.body:
## Why

First matching rule wins. `allow('*')` then `deny('customers.export')` means the deny never runs. `nominee check` today only reports tool names that miss the built-in sample list ([`packages/cli/src/check.ts`](packages/cli/src/check.ts)) — it does not warn about shadowing.

The existing unreachable-name fixture is [`packages/cli/test/fixtures/unreachable-policy.mjs`](packages/cli/test/fixtures/unreachable-policy.mjs).

## Pointer

- Logic: [`packages/cli/src/check.ts`](packages/cli/src/check.ts)
- Tests: [`packages/cli/test/check.test.ts`](packages/cli/test/check.test.ts)
- Add a fixture e.g. `packages/cli/test/fixtures/shadowed-rule.mjs`

## Acceptance criterion

Given:

```js
export default {
  rules: [
    { effect: 'allow', tools: ['*'] },
    { effect: 'deny', tools: ['customers.export'] },
  ],
  fallback: 'deny',
}
```

`runCheck` exits `1` and prints that `deny:customers.export` is shadowed by an earlier rule (name the earlier `allow:*`). A policy where `deny('customers.export')` comes **first** still exits `0`.

Do not execute `when` predicates (same limitation as today).

issues.title: `nominee check`: fixture for wildcard-only vs typo that has no Levenshtein hint
issues.body:
## Why

`nearestSampleTool` in [`packages/cli/src/check.ts`](packages/cli/src/check.ts) suppresses suggestions when edit distance is large. There is a test for `emial.send` → `email.read`, but none for a pattern that should **not** suggest, and none for a legitimate wildcard like `refund.*` that matches nothing in `SAMPLE_TOOLS`.

## Pointer

- [`packages/cli/src/check.ts`](packages/cli/src/check.ts) (`SAMPLE_TOOLS`, `nearestSampleTool`)
- [`packages/cli/test/check.test.ts`](packages/cli/test/check.test.ts)
- New fixtures under `packages/cli/test/fixtures/`

## Acceptance criterion

1. A fixture whose only rule is `allow('refund.issue')` exits `1`, reports never-matched, and does **not** print `did you mean` (distance above threshold).
2. Optionally: if you add `refund.issue` to `SAMPLE_TOOLS` instead, document the list in [`packages/cli/README.md`](packages/cli/README.md) and make the existing misspelling test still pass.

Pick one approach in the PR description. Prefer (1) if you do not want to expand the sample set.

issues.title: `nominee check --tools`: extra sample tool names for reachability
issues.body:
## Why

`SAMPLE_TOOLS` in [`packages/cli/src/check.ts`](packages/cli/src/check.ts) is a fixed list (`email.read`, `github.merge_pr`, …). A real policy named `refund.issue` is reported unreachable even when it is the whole product.

## Pointer

- CLI entry: [`packages/cli/src/index.ts`](packages/cli/src/index.ts) (or wherever `check` is dispatched)
- [`packages/cli/src/check.ts`](packages/cli/src/check.ts)
- Tests: [`packages/cli/test/check.test.ts`](packages/cli/test/check.test.ts)
- Docs: [`packages/cli/README.md`](packages/cli/README.md)

## Acceptance criterion

`runCheck(file, { tools: ['refund.issue'] })` (or argv `--tools=refund.issue`) treats `refund.issue` as a sample call. A policy of `allow('refund.issue')` then exits `0`. Built-in samples remain unless the caller replaces them — document which.

No network. Core stays untouched.

issues.title: Add `formatReceiptsCsv` (or `toCSV`) next to `toJSONL` / `formatReceipts`
issues.body:
## Why

Operators paste receipt chains into spreadsheets. Today we have compact text (`formatReceipts`) and JSONL (`ReceiptLedger.toJSONL`) in [`packages/core/src/receipt.ts`](packages/core/src/receipt.ts). CSV of the non-sensitive columns would make an audit export without inventing a new store.

## Pointer

- [`packages/core/src/receipt.ts`](packages/core/src/receipt.ts)
- Export from [`packages/core/src/index.ts`](packages/core/src/index.ts)
- Tests: [`packages/core/test/receipt.test.ts`](packages/core/test/receipt.test.ts)

## Acceptance criterion

Export a function that writes CSV with at least: `seq,at,type,user,tool,effect,decision,rule,reason,inputHash,prev,hash`.

- Escape commas/quotes in `reason`.
- Do **not** include raw `input` or tokens even if `inputMode` was `'raw'`.
- Round-trip test: parse the CSV, `verifyReceipts` still works on the original array (CSV is a projection, not a replacement for JSON).
- One-line mention in [`packages/core/README.md`](packages/core/README.md).

Call the chain **tamper-evident**, never tamper-proof.

issues.title: Optional `reason` (and `rule`) in `formatReceipts` compact output
issues.body:
## Why

[`formatReceipts`](packages/core/src/receipt.ts) prints `#seq type tool outcome hash[:12]`. Denials without `reason` are hard to skim in a terminal. The CLI proof already cares about human-readable receipts.

## Pointer

- [`packages/core/src/receipt.ts`](packages/core/src/receipt.ts) (`formatReceipts`)
- [`packages/core/test/receipt.test.ts`](packages/core/test/receipt.test.ts)

## Acceptance criterion

Either:

- append `rule` and `reason` when present, truncated to a sane width, or
- `formatReceipts(receipts, { verbose: true })` for the extra columns.

Existing default snapshot/string assertions in `receipt.test.ts` must stay stable **or** be updated in the same PR. Prefer an opt-in flag if the current string is treated as a contract.

issues.title: Docs: AI SDK integration still uses `parameters` instead of `inputSchema`
issues.body:
## Why

[`docs/integrations/ai-sdk.md`](docs/integrations/ai-sdk.md) shows `tool({ parameters: z.object(...) })`. Current Vercel AI SDK tools use `inputSchema`. Copy-pasting the guide fails typecheck on `ai@5+` / `ai@7`.

Same smell in [`docs/integrations/openai-agents.md`](docs/integrations/openai-agents.md) if that SDK has moved — check before changing it.

## Pointer

- [`docs/integrations/ai-sdk.md`](docs/integrations/ai-sdk.md)
- Cross-check [`packages/ai/README.md`](packages/ai/README.md) and [`packages/ai/test`](packages/ai/test) for the live shape

## Acceptance criterion

- The AI SDK snippet type-checks against the peer range declared in `packages/ai/package.json`.
- `guardTools` / `nominee.run()` wording stays; do not revive `authorize()` as the execution path (see `brand/check-surfaces.mjs`).
- Do not edit `site/index.html`, `llms.txt`, `site/llms.txt`, or `brand/content.ts`.

issues.title: Docs: list `nominee check` sample tools and the `when`-not-executed limitation
issues.body:
## Why

[`packages/cli/README.md`](packages/cli/README.md) already says `when` is not executed, but the **exact** `SAMPLE_TOOLS` list lives only in [`packages/cli/src/check.ts`](packages/cli/src/check.ts). Contributors invent `refund.issue` policies, run `check`, and think the CLI is broken.

## Pointer

- [`packages/cli/README.md`](packages/cli/README.md)
- Optionally one sentence in [`docs/production.md`](docs/production.md) **only if** you already have that file open — do not expand scope

## Acceptance criterion

README contains the full current `SAMPLE_TOOLS` list (keep it in sync with `check.ts` — if you change the list, change both). Explicit note: a well-formed `allow('refund.issue')` is reported unreachable against the built-in samples. Point to Discussions for questions.

issues.title: Example: tiny Express/standalone `run()` snippet in `docs/integrations/standalone.md`
issues.body:
## Why

[`docs/integrations/standalone.md`](docs/integrations/standalone.md) is the non-framework path. Newcomers wrapping a plain function (not an SDK `tool()`) still need to see `nominee.run({ tool, input, user }, execute)` rather than `authorize()` then a bare call.

## Pointer

- [`docs/integrations/standalone.md`](docs/integrations/standalone.md)
- Mirror the contract in [`.github/CONTRIBUTING.md`](.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) (decision-bound execution)

## Acceptance criterion

One copy-pasteable TypeScript snippet: default-deny policy, `ask` on a write tool, `run()` around a fake `issueRefund`. Mention that `production: true` needs durable stores (`nominee-postgres`). No new package. Do not touch guarded brand surfaces (`site/index.html`, `llms.txt`, `brand/content.ts`).

issues.title: Track remaining adapter compatibility work from #48
issues.body:
## Why

#48 was closed in the August 2026 triage. [`docs/adapter-compatibility.md`](docs/adapter-compatibility.md) still flags real follow-ups: CJS `nominee-ai` vs `ai@7` on older Node, open-ended peer floors on mastra/mcp/openai, and adapters whose unit tests still call `execute` with `as never` fakes.

This issue is the tracker so the repo does not look finished.

## Pointer

- [`docs/adapter-compatibility.md`](docs/adapter-compatibility.md)
- Compat tests: `packages/ai/test/ai.compat.test.ts`, `packages/eve/test/eve.compat.test.ts`

## Acceptance criterion (split PRs are fine)

Pick **one**:

1. Document the `ai@7` CJS trap in `packages/ai/README.md` with the Node version floor, or stop shipping a CJS entry that `require('ai')`s an ESM-only peer.
2. Add an upper bound **or** a CI job that fails when a peer major is published and the compat test cannot be imported.

Not a good-first-issue if you take (1) as a packaging change — say so in the PR.

issues.title: Track remaining security-review discipline from #51
issues.body:
## Why

#51 was closed; [`docs/security-review-checklist.md`](docs/security-review-checklist.md) exists. Remaining work from triage: attacker models, non-goals, and claim-to-test traceability so we never ship "stops prompt injection" / "tamper-proof" / "compliance-ready".

## Pointer

- [`docs/security-review-checklist.md`](docs/security-review-checklist.md)
- [`docs/positioning.md`](docs/positioning.md) (prohibited claims)
- [`security-contract/contract.test.ts`](security-contract/contract.test.ts)

## Acceptance criterion

Add a short "Non-goals / prohibited claims" section to the checklist that maps each prohibited phrase to the test or doc that forbids it. Optional: one CI grep in `brand/check-surfaces.mjs` **or** a tiny script that fails if `site/blog` or READMEs contain `tamper-proof` / `compliance-ready` / `stops prompt injection`.

If you add a grep, keep `site/blog/` included — that is where overclaims hurt most.

issues.title: Track remaining comparison-proof work from #53
issues.body:
## Why

#53 asked for developer-facing comparison articles. Several essays already live under `site/blog/` (`native-approval-vs-action-authorization`, `oauth-scopes-vs-action-authorization`, `fga-opa-decide-nominee-executes`). Bottom-of-funnel how-tos are a separate Linear ticket (NOM-15).

## Pointer

- [`docs/competitive-map.md`](docs/competitive-map.md)
- [`site/blog/`](site/blog/)

## Acceptance criterion

Add a table at the top of `docs/competitive-map.md` linking each comparison axis to the live essay URL. Note gaps (no LangChain adapter essay yet). Do not edit `brand/content.ts` or `site/index.html`.

issues.title: Track remaining partner-kit gaps from #54
issues.body:
## Why

#54 was closed after adding kits under [`docs/partner-kits/`](docs/partner-kits/). Remaining: keep kits honest ("not a replacement for") and executable where we claim they are.

## Pointer

- [`docs/partner-kits/auth0.md`](docs/partner-kits/auth0.md)
- [`docs/partner-kits/workos-fga.md`](docs/partner-kits/workos-fga.md)
- [`docs/partner-kits/opa.md`](docs/partner-kits/opa.md)
- [`docs/partner-kits/arcade-composio.md`](docs/partner-kits/arcade-composio.md)
- Recipes: `examples/opa-recipe`, `examples/fga-recipe`

## Acceptance criterion

For **one** kit: add a "Runnable?" line that is either a relative path to an example that `pnpm --filter` tests, or an explicit "illustrative only". Fix any kit that currently implies a runnable server that is not in the repo.
